newsitem.title: USA: Georgia indicators signal growth in New Year.
newsitem.headline: Georgia indicators signal growth in New Year.

text.p: Georgia's Composite Index of Leading Economic Indicators rose for the fifth consecutive month in November, signaling anew that the state's economy will keep growing in the new year, state Labor Commissioner David Poythress said in his monthly report.
Leading indicators, designed to forecast economic activity six months ahead, rose 0.11 points to 144.59 on a 1988 index base of 100.
The state's Composite Index of Coincident indicators rose 0.22 points to 144.99 on a 1987 base of 100. That index is designed to measure current conditions.

The leading indicators were pushed upward in November by an increase in the manufacturing workweek and a drop in initial jobless claims. On the downside, residential building permits, new motor vehicle titles and new business incorporations declined.
The average manufacturing workweek increased by six minutes to 44.2 hours in November, while first-time jobless claims dropped by 5.31 percent from October to 28,394.
Continuing unemployment claims edged up to 162,053 in November, a gain of 1.52 percent over October.
The state issued 40,460 titles for new motor vehicles in November, down 8.43 percent from October. Residential construction permits dipped to 5,959, down 2.93 percent from October.
State revenue collections declined to $865.9 million in November, down 1.59 percent for the month but up 4.88 percent over the year.

Nonfarm employment increaased by 9,000 jobs to a record high of 3.57 million as the Christams shopping season got under way. The work force is expected to show another jump for December before taking a fall in January, Poythress said.
Georgia's unemployment rate in November was 4.5 percent, up from 4.3 percent in October but down from 4.7 percent a year ago.
